why.headline: A still, balanced set lets you push off either way.

claims.text: In adult keepers, moving early let fake kicks fool them.
In elite adult keepers, too much early hip turning slowed weaker-side dives.
Young elite players did reaction drills twice a week. After 6 weeks, reaction runs were 7.7 to 9.4% faster.
Early-teen players swapped some football drills for jumps and footwork. After 8 weeks, sprint and agility tests were 2.1 to 9.6% faster.

keep_up.text: Keep training it every week to keep gains coming. In one youth study, jump gains lasted 8 weeks after training stopped. Everyone improves at their own pace.

map.plain: The big muscles at the front of your thighs
Your calf muscles, which hold your heels up

note.text: No study measured muscles in the ready stance. These come from adult squat studies and the card.

claims.text: In a youth trial, drills with a signal improved reaction runs most. Plain turning drills improved plain turns most.
For adult keepers, the kicker's late cues were the useful ones. Staying set lets you use them.

limits.text: No study has tested holding the ready stance as a drill. The youth trials trained jumps, sprints and footwork.
